task.description: WF-01 Step 3: register each requirement REQ-VALIDATOR passed in letflow-queue via register_task, and write each response's impl_order back into docs/requirements.yaml. Per WF-01's ISS-0221 note this step is not optional -- a requirement that passed Step 2 but was never registered is well-formed, validated and permanently unclaimable, because get_next_task is the only sanctioned selection path and register_task is impl_order's only source.
acceptance_criteria: Every requirement that passed Step 2 was actually registered -- not just drafted and validated.
impl_order in docs/requirements.yaml matches the queue's response for that requirement, not a guess.
If the queue was unreachable, that is stated explicitly rather than silently skipped.

result.summary: All 19 requirements REQ-185..REQ-203 registered in letflow-queue as tasks 358-376, and each impl_order written back into docs/requirements.yaml from register_task's actual response. Registration ran in TOPOLOGICAL ORDER because TASK_QUEUE.md establishes that depends_on takes integer queue task ids rather than REQ- strings, so a requirement whose dependency is not yet registered cannot be registered either; every dependency edge therefore resolved to a real id, mixing this batch's newly-assigned ids with the already-known ids of earlier requirements (e.g. REQ-190 -> task 363 with deps [362, 139, 354, 356]). Mapping: REQ-185=358, REQ-186=359, REQ-187=360, REQ-188=361, REQ-189=362, REQ-190=363, REQ-191=364, REQ-192=365, REQ-193=366, REQ-194=367, REQ-195=368, REQ-196=369, REQ-197=370, REQ-198=371, REQ-199=372, REQ-200=373, REQ-201=374, REQ-202=375, REQ-203=376. No id was guessed or derived -- per TASK_QUEUE.md a fabricated impl_order doubles as a working /tasks/<id>/ URL addressing an unrelated real task, which closed the wrong GitHub issue once before (ISS-0092/GH#314). Registration used curl rather than a Python HTTP client, because Cloudflare fronts this service and rejects urllib's default user-agent with 403 / error code 1010. The write-back into docs/requirements.yaml was a pure textual 19-line insert (one impl_order line after each entry's stage: line, matching the existing convention including the trailing '# letflow-queue task id' comment) so the rest of the file stayed byte-identical -- confirmed by git diff --stat showing 19 insertions and 0 deletions. Note the queue exposes no GET-by-id endpoint (deliberately four operations per its README's Design section), so register_task's own responses are the authoritative record of the assigned ids; a GET /tasks/<id> probe returns 404 by design and is not evidence of a failed registration. Verified afterwards with the repository's own purpose-built gates, run after mix deps.get: `mix letflow.check_requirements_registration` reports '177 entries = 177 registered + 0 deferred + 0 neither + 0 unclassified', and `mix letflow.check_deferral_staleness` reports '0 deferred of 177 entries; 0 stale'. Independently re-checked before committing: 177 entries parse, zero duplicate ids, zero orphaned depends_on, zero dependency cycles, and every impl_order in the file equals the id the queue actually returned. Separately, queue task 356 (REQ-183, first batch) remains LOCKED to this host, deliberately: REQ-VALIDATOR confirmed REQ-183 is unimplementable as originally drafted, and although REQ-183 has now been amended and gains a depends_on edge on REQ-189 (task 362) which the queue's dependency gating will enforce, the lock was left in place as a belt-and-braces guard and is the one piece of queue state this run leaves held.
